items.quote: The purpose of this policy is to outline the processes related to responding to sexualized violence or misconduct.
items.reason: The policy is a stand-alone document with its own processes and procedures for responding to sexualized violence.
The policy does not mention any commitment to posting the policy publicly or on the website.

items.quote: If someone has experienced or witnessed sexualized violence or misconduct, they can talk to someone at the College to get help, advice, information, or to be referred to other resources.
items.reason: Reporting is mentioned, but the policy does not outline clear, concrete steps or specific contact details for how to file a report.
The policy does not address the complainant's past sexual history.
The policy does not address protecting the complainant from face-to-face contact with the respondent.
The policy does not address whether complainants are permitted or forbidden to speak about their experience.

items.quote: A person may report an incident of sexualized violence or misconduct to the police anytime.
items.reason: The policy mentions the option of reporting to the police, but does not explicitly state that the choice of which process to pursue is entirely up to the complainant.

items.quote: The College recognizes that some individuals may hesitate to disclose or make a complaint about incidents of sexualized violence or misconduct; anyone may freely and safely disclose cases involving alcohol, drugs, involvement in sex work, or any other behavior.
items.reason: The policy explicitly guarantees that individuals can safely disclose incidents involving alcohol or drugs.
The policy does not specify any binding timelines for the complaint or investigation process.

items.quote: The College may implement interim measures while it assesses or investigates a report of sexualized violence or misconduct, or where interim measures are deemed necessary.
items.reason: The implementation of interim measures is discretionary, as indicated by the word 'may'.

items.quote: This policy applies to sexualized violence or misconduct that is alleged to have occurred: a) on or off Langara College premises, including technology-facilitated behaviour, or at College-sponsored academic, athletic, or social events, and where the interaction between the individuals involved is an extension of their relationship to Langara College;
items.reason: Off-campus activities are covered generally, but co-op, internships, or work placements are not explicitly mentioned.

items.quote: Both the person who experienced the sexualized violence or misconduct and the respondent will receive a verbal summary of the investigation findings.
items.reason: The policy commits to sharing a verbal summary of the findings, which is a limited form of informing the complainant of the outcome.
The policy does not address public annual reporting of sexual violence statistics.
The policy indicates a review cycle of three years (from 2023 to 2026), which is longer than two years.
The policy does not address student representation on policy review committees.

items.quote: The College will provide education and training to students and employees to increase awareness of sexualized violence, misconduct, and rape culture, prevent incidents, and promote effective responses to sexualized violence or misconduct.
items.reason: Training is mentioned generally for students and employees, but there is no mandatory trauma-informed training requirement specified for investigators or decision-makers.

items.quote: The College will provide education and training to students and employees to increase awareness of sexualized violence, misconduct, and rape culture, prevent incidents, and promote effective responses to sexualized violence or misconduct.
items.reason: The policy commits to providing education and training to students to prevent incidents of sexualized violence.
